sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Estet Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的埃斯特·赫恩登。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, over the past decade, medical companies have begun offering pregnant women new screening tests that promised to detect rare genetic disorders in their fetuses.
sentences.zh: 今天，在过去十年里，医疗公司开始为孕妇提供新的筛查测试，声称可以检测出胎儿罕见的遗传疾病。

sentences.en: What those women weren't told was that if they tested positive, there would be a high likelihood that the result would be wrong.
sentences.zh: 但这些女性没有被告知的是，如果她们的检测结果呈阳性，结果很可能是错误的。

sentences.en: A Times investigation reveals how tests that promise peace of mind have instead caused anguish and confusion.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一项调查揭示了这些承诺带来“安心”的测试，反而造成了痛苦和困惑。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Sarah Cliff.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事萨拉·克里夫。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, January 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月4日，星期二。

sentences.en: So, Sarah, how did you come to this story?
sentences.zh: 那么，萨拉，你是怎么接触到这个故事的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I usually cover medical billing for The Times, and readers often send me odd, surprising bills they've received.
sentences.zh: 是的，我通常负责《纽约时报》的医疗账单报道，读者经常会发给我一些他们收到的奇怪、令人惊讶的账单。

sentences.en: And I'd received a handful for this certain type of prenatal teSt.
sentences.zh: 我收到过几份关于这种特定产前检查的账单。

sentences.en: And they were hundreds to thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 金额从几百到几千美元不等。

sentences.en: So I was looking into the bill, and my editor suggested just looking into what these tests are in the first place.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始调查这些账单，我的编辑建议我先从了解这些测试本身是什么开始。

sentences.en: So I just started doing the basic research that I usually do, reading some academic studies, looking through people's experiences with them online.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始做我通常会做的基础研究，阅读一些学术研究，并在网上浏览人们的使用体验。

sentences.en: And I came across a Reddit community focused on this type of screening and just kept seeing the same kind of story repeated again and again,
sentences.zh: 我偶然发现了一个专注于此类筛查的Reddit社区，并不断看到同样的故事反复出现，

sentences.en: where someone who was pregnant went to the doctor, took this particular type of screening test, and was really surprised to get a positive result for a disorder
sentences.zh: 即某位孕妇去看医生，做了这种特定的筛查测试，结果对一种她从未听说过的疾病呈阳性，这让她非常惊讶。

sentences.en: they had never heard of.
sentences.zh: （接上句）她从未听说过的疾病。

sentences.en: And they, you know, often talked about a really agonizing month between this first screening and a follow-up test that was either going to confirm or disprove the original results.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，她们经常谈到在第一次筛查和后续确认或推翻原始结果的测试之间，那段非常痛苦的月份。

sentences.en: And in the end, it turned out that the original test was wrong, and there's actually nothing wrong with the pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 最终结果证明，最初的测试是错误的，怀孕其实没有任何问题。

sentences.en: And they went on to have babies without the conditions that they had screened positive for.
sentences.zh: 她们后来生下的孩子并没有她们筛查出阳性的那些疾病。

sentences.en: And so that kind of, you know, piqued my interest a little bit to think, you know, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 所以这引起了我的兴趣，我想，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And why are so many women reporting this type of story?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么多女性都在报告这类故事？

sentences.en: So what exactly is this test?
sentences.zh: 那么这到底是什么测试？

sentences.en: So this test, it's known as a few things.
sentences.zh: 这种测试有几种叫法。

sentences.en: It's known as cell-free DNA screening or non-invasive prenatal testing.
sentences.zh: 它被称为无创DNA筛查或无创产前检测。

sentences.en: And it's usually drawn at a doctor's office or a laboratory.
sentences.zh: 通常是在医生办公室或实验室进行抽血。

sentences.en: And this is a test that screens for chromosomal abnormalities in a fetus.
sentences.zh: 这是一种筛查胎儿染色体异常的测试。

sentences.en: And before this test existed, this was done, you know, with a number of ultrasounds, a number of blood draws over multiple prenatal visits to mostly screen for Down syndrome.
sentences.zh: 在这种测试出现之前，这通常是通过多次超声波检查和多次产前就诊时的抽血来完成的，主要用于筛查唐氏综合征。

sentences.en: And they produced a decent number of false positives.
sentences.zh: 而且它们产生了一定数量的假阳性结果。

sentences.en: And then about 10 years ago, this test comes along.
sentences.zh: 大约10年前，这种测试出现了。

sentences.en: It can be done at 10 weeks.
sentences.zh: 它可以在怀孕10周时进行。

sentences.en: It just requires one blood draw.
sentences.zh: 只需要抽一次血。

sentences.en: And it turns out to be really quite accurate at screening for Down syndrome.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，它在筛查唐氏综合征方面非常准确。

sentences.en: And it's a pretty remarkable advancement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当了不起的进步。

sentences.en: So with these tests, well-received, it seems as if they are providing a real niche to streamline that screening process.
sentences.zh: 既然这些测试广受好评，看起来它们确实在简化筛查流程方面发挥了独特的作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, they really are.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Obstetricians are happy with them because they feel like they are able to provide a service to their patients.
sentences.zh: 产科医生对它们很满意，因为他们觉得能够为患者提供一种服务。

sentences.en: They're not having to do as many invasive procedures like an amniocentesis.
sentences.zh: 他们不必再做那么多像羊膜穿刺术这样的侵入性手术了。

sentences.en: So they're pretty happy with the technology.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对这项技术相当满意。

sentences.en: Patients are happy with it because it can also screen for what your baby's sex is at 10 weeks.
sentences.zh: 患者也很满意，因为它还可以在10周时筛查出胎儿的性别。

sentences.en: That's something you, before this, couldn't know until about 20 weeks pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，你直到怀孕20周左右才能知道这一点。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So obstetricians found patients were coming into their offices, you know, asking, I want the test that screens for sex.
sentences.zh: 所以产科医生发现患者来到办公室时会问：“我想要那个能筛查性别的测试。”

sentences.en: So they were quite well-received.
sentences.zh: 所以它们非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And you saw companies realizing there was a market in this type of testing.
sentences.zh: 你看到公司意识到这类测试存在市场。

sentences.en: About 4 million women give birth each year.
sentences.zh: 每年约有400万女性分娩。

sentences.en: And that was 4 million women who could, you know, potentially use this type of screening product.
sentences.zh: 这意味着有400万女性可能使用这种筛查产品。

sentences.en: So after the first test launches in 2011, you really quickly see about a half dozen other companies trying to get into this space.
sentences.zh: 因此，在2011年第一项测试推出后，你很快就会看到大约六家其他公司试图进入这个领域。

sentences.en: Some of them are big laboratory companies like LabCorp, for example, which buys a test called Maternity 21 from a smaller biotech startup.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是大型实验室公司，例如LabCorp，它从一家小型生物技术初创公司购买了一种名为Maternity 21的测试。

sentences.en: A company called Natera gets into this space and they quickly become the market leader,
sentences.zh: 一家名为Natera的公司进入了这个领域，并迅速成为市场领导者，

sentences.en: Quest Diagnostics, Myriad.
sentences.zh: 还有Quest Diagnostics和Myriad。

sentences.en: These are all different companies getting into the space.
sentences.zh: 这些都是进入该领域的不同公司。

sentences.en: And they are looking at ways to differentiate their products.
sentences.zh: 他们正在寻找使产品差异化的方法。

sentences.en: And one of the things that starts to happen is they start screening for conditions that are rarer than Down syndrome.
sentences.zh: 开始发生的事情之一是，他们开始筛查比唐氏综合征更罕见的疾病。

sentences.en: They start with something called trisomy 13 and trisomy 18.
sentences.zh: 他们从所谓的13-三体和18-三体开始。

sentences.en: And then they move into a new category of testing for micro-deletions, which are kind of small missing pieces of chromosomes.
sentences.zh: 然后他们进入了一个新的测试类别，即微缺失，这是一种染色体的小片段缺失。

sentences.en: And those micro-deletions are sometimes associated with certain syndromes.
sentences.zh: 这些微缺失有时与某些综合征有关。

sentences.en: Some of the better-known ones are DeGeorge syndrome, which becomes a screening,
sentences.zh: 一些比较知名的包括迪乔治综合征，它成为了筛查项目，

sentences.en: Creta Schott, Engelman, and Prader-Willi.
sentences.zh: 还有猫叫综合征、天使人综合征和普拉德-威利综合征。

sentences.en: They tend to be pretty rare.
sentences.zh: 它们往往非常罕见。

sentences.en: So they are often not familiar to patients, but these are the things that are starting to be added on to this type of screening.
sentences.zh: 因此，患者通常不熟悉这些疾病，但这些正是开始被添加到此类筛查中的内容。

sentences.en: They also get marketed directly to patients, directly to doctors as quite accurate products.
sentences.zh: 它们还被直接向患者和医生推销为非常准确的产品。

sentences.en: You start seeing language like total confidence in every result or information for your peace of mind.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到诸如“对每一个结果充满信心”或“为您带来安心的信息”之类的宣传语。

sentences.en: They say they're going to give you clear answers, clear positives and negatives, and kind of information you can truSt.
sentences.zh: 他们说会给你明确的答案，明确的阳性和阴性结果，以及你可以信任的信息。

sentences.en: And you get to the point where in 2020, a third of pregnant women, that's over a million people, are getting the down screening with the sex tests.
sentences.zh: 到了2020年，三分之一的孕妇，即超过一百万人，都在进行这种带有性别测试的筛查。

sentences.en: Some share of those, we don't know exactly how many, are getting the expanded tests that are looking for the rarer conditions.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分人，我们不知道具体有多少，正在进行寻找更罕见疾病的扩展测试。

sentences.en: But the problem that I found in my reporting is when it comes to those newer expanded tests, the problem is that the positive results on those tests, they are often wrong.
sentences.zh: 但在我的报道中发现的问题是，当涉及到那些较新的扩展测试时，问题在于这些测试的阳性结果往往是错误的。

sentences.en: So what exactly did you find?
sentences.zh: 那么你到底发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so before I get into the findings, I think it's just important to have some context.
sentences.zh: 是的，在进入调查结果之前，我认为了解一些背景很重要。

sentences.en: One is that the test is still quite reliable for Down syndrome when it's screening for that condition.
sentences.zh: 第一，当筛查唐氏综合征时，这种测试仍然相当可靠。

sentences.en: And second, most people who take this test are going to screen negative on it.
sentences.zh: 第二，大多数进行此项测试的人结果会呈阴性。

sentences.en: Most people will not get a positive result.
sentences.zh: 大多数人不会得到阳性结果。

sentences.en: But for the people who do get a positive result, there's about a half dozen tests where we found that those positive results are wrong about 85% of the time.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些确实得到阳性结果的人来说，我们发现大约有六种测试，其阳性结果约85%是错误的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, we were talking about testing for rare conditions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们谈论的是罕见疾病的测试。

sentences.en: So as you're saying, most of these are going to come negative.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，大多数结果会是阴性。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But for the positive ones, you're saying as many as more than 80% of them,
sentences.zh: 但对于阳性结果，你是说高达80%以上，

sentences.en: 80 out of 100 of those positive tests could be incorrect?
sentences.zh: 100个阳性测试中有80个可能是错误的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the numbers can get even higher.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字甚至可能更高。

sentences.en: There's one test we looked at for a condition that occurs in about 1 in 20,000 births.
sentences.zh: 我们研究过一种针对大约2万分之一出生率疾病的测试。

sentences.en: We found that 93% of the positive results for that test turn out to be wrong on further testing.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，该测试93%的阳性结果在进一步检查后被证明是错误的。

sentences.en: So it's a pretty big share.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个相当大的比例。

sentences.en: And again, these are the tests that are being sold in that marketing that is talking about total confidence, peace of mind, clear results.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这些测试在营销中被宣传为“充满信心”、“安心”、“结果明确”。

sentences.en: These are some of the tests being sold with that type of language.
sentences.zh: 这些就是用这类语言推销的一些测试。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《纽约时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Sarah, so you said a lot of these positive tests end up being wrong.
sentences.zh: 萨拉，你说很多这些阳性测试结果最终都是错误的。

sentences.en: Why are they so wrong?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们会这么不准？

sentences.en: How is this happening?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: It mostly has to do with the fact that these are pretty rare conditions.
sentences.zh: 这主要与这些是相当罕见的疾病有关。

sentences.en: These are conditions that occur in maybe one in 4,000 to at the rarest, one in 100,000 births.
sentences.zh: 这些疾病的发生率可能在四千分之一到最罕见的十万分之一之间。

sentences.en: And when you have a rare condition, this isn't just true in prenatal testing, it's true in a lot of testing, when you have a rare condition, you're likely going to generate
sentences.zh: 当你面对一种罕见疾病时，这不仅适用于产前检测，也适用于许多其他检测，当你面对罕见疾病时，你很可能会产生

sentences.en: more false positives than true ones because you're just looking for something that doesn't exist a lot.
sentences.zh: 更多的假阳性而非真阳性，因为你只是在寻找一种并不常见的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Needle in a haystack.
sentences.zh: 大海捞针。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And so you find a lot of hay in the haystack when you are just looking for that one needle.
sentences.zh: 所以当你只是在寻找那根针时，你会发现干草堆里有很多干草。

sentences.en: Do the companies know about any of this?
sentences.zh: 这些公司知道这一切吗？

sentences.en: They have marketed themselves as the ones who can identify these rare genetic conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们将自己推销为能够识别这些罕见遗传疾病的公司。

sentences.en: But what we're seeing from these test results are that the positive results are often not true.
sentences.zh: 但从这些测试结果中我们看到，阳性结果往往不是真的。

sentences.en: Did they know that before you did?
sentences.zh: 在你发现之前他们知道吗？

sentences.en: Some of them did, and they certainly could have because the way that we did our research was essentially looking for any study we could find in the academic world,
sentences.zh: 有些人知道，他们当然可以知道，因为我们进行研究的方式本质上是寻找我们在学术界能找到的任何研究，

sentences.en: outside the academic world, that had looked at how well these tests work.
sentences.zh: 以及学术界之外，那些研究过这些测试效果如何的研究。

sentences.en: And we eventually found about a half dozen studies in this space.
sentences.zh: 我们最终在这个领域找到了大约六项研究。

sentences.en: Some were conducted by testing companies themselves, other by independent academic researchers.
sentences.zh: 有些是由测试公司自己进行的，另一些是由独立的学术研究人员进行的。

sentences.en: And working with a few experts in this space, we developed some methods to combine all those findings and kind of produce the most comprehensive look that we could
sentences.zh: 通过与该领域的一些专家合作，我们开发了一些方法来结合所有这些发现，并尽可能全面地呈现

sentences.en: at how well these positive results are doing.
sentences.zh: 这些阳性结果的表现如何。

sentences.en: And so the data we have is all public.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有的数据都是公开的。

sentences.en: It's all out there.
sentences.zh: 它们都在那里。

sentences.en: You know, we took the time to sift through it and combine it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们花时间仔细筛选并整合了它们。

sentences.en: And that's how we got to our findings about how many of these positive results turn out to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们得出关于有多少阳性结果最终是错误的研究结果的方法。

sentences.en: I know that you've owned the medical billing.
sentences.zh: 我知道你一直负责医疗账单报道。

sentences.en: B, these companies, I'm sure, are frightened at the idea of a Sarah Cliff email.
sentences.zh: B，这些公司，我相信，对萨拉·克里夫的邮件感到恐惧。

sentences.en: But what did they actually say when you took your findings to them?
sentences.zh: 但当你把你的发现告诉他们时，他们实际上说了什么？

sentences.en: So they said, you know, many acknowledged our findings and said that they still believe there's value in this type of screening test because it is picking up the true positives,
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，许多人承认了我们的发现，并表示他们仍然认为这种筛查测试有价值，因为它确实能发现真阳性，

sentences.en: that it is finding some of these cases of disorders that parents would not have known about otherwise, and that they said they try their best to be very, very clear
sentences.zh: 它确实发现了一些父母原本不会知道的疾病病例，他们说他们尽最大努力非常、非常明确地说明

sentences.en: that it is a screening teSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一种筛查测试。

sentences.en: It is not a diagnostic teSt.
sentences.zh: 它不是诊断测试。

sentences.en: The patient should be counseled on this test before.
sentences.zh: 患者在测试前应该接受咨询。

sentences.en: So essentially be told, here's what a positive result would mean for you.
sentences.zh: 也就是被告知，阳性结果对你意味着什么。

sentences.en: So they are making the case that these tests are doing more good by identifying cases of disease.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为，通过识别疾病病例，这些测试带来的好处更多。

sentences.en: But that experience they talk about, how each patient should be counseled, how they should give consent for these tests, that was really different than the experience I heard about
sentences.zh: 但他们谈论的那种体验，即每位患者应该如何接受咨询，如何为这些测试提供知情同意，这与我采访的经历截然不同，

sentences.en: interviewing, you know, more than a dozen women who had received a positive result that turned out to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 我采访了十多位收到阳性结果但后来证明是错误的女性。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what I was going to ask.
sentences.zh: 是的，我正想问这个。

sentences.en: What is the experience of these women who are getting the positive results?
sentences.zh: 那些得到阳性结果的女性有什么样的经历？

sentences.en: Because of course, when they receive that test result, they don't know it's a false positive, right?
sentences.zh: 因为当然，当她们收到那个测试结果时，她们不知道那是假阳性，对吧？

sentences.en: So how does what is seemingly very, very bad news being received by these women?
sentences.zh: 那么这些女性是如何接受这看似非常、非常糟糕的消息的？

sentences.en: I had, you know, multiple women describe this as the worst time of their lives, the time between when they received this result and when they later learned
sentences.zh: 我有多位女性将其描述为她们一生中最糟糕的时刻，即她们收到这个结果到后来得知

sentences.en: that the result was wrong.
sentences.zh: 结果是错误的那段时间。

sentences.en: And, you know, I met a lot of these women through the Reddit forum I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我通过我之前提到的Reddit论坛认识了许多这样的女性。

sentences.en: One that really stands out to me is a woman named Yael Geller who, you know, spent a year of fertility treatments trying to get pregnant with their second child
sentences.zh: 其中一个让我印象深刻的是一位名叫耶尔·盖勒的女性，你知道，她花了一年时间进行生育治疗，试图怀上第二个孩子，

sentences.en: and was so, so excited when her pregnancy test was positive.
sentences.zh: 当她的怀孕测试呈阳性时，她非常、非常兴奋。

sentences.en: You know, she had a normal ultrasound, she told her three-year-old about this brother or sister that was in her tummy.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，她做过正常的超声波检查，还告诉她三岁的孩子，肚子里有个小弟弟或小妹妹。

sentences.en: It seemed like everything was finally working.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎终于步入正轨了。

sentences.en: And she is driving her son home from school one day when she gets this call saying she had screened positive for a condition, you know, she didn't even know
sentences.zh: 有一天她开车送儿子放学回家，接到一个电话，说她的一项筛查结果呈阳性，而她甚至不知道

sentences.en: she was being screened for.
sentences.zh: 自己接受了这项筛查。

sentences.en: It's called Prader-Willi syndrome.
sentences.zh: 这叫普拉德-威利综合征（Prader-Willi syndrome）。

sentences.en: And it's a pretty serious condition.
sentences.zh: 这是一种相当严重的疾病。

sentences.en: You know, she starts doing a lot of research, a lot of Googling.
sentences.zh: 她开始做大量的研究，在谷歌上疯狂搜索。

sentences.en: She'd never heard of this before.
sentences.zh: 她以前从未听说过这个病。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 是啊，

sentences.en: I've never heard of this either.
sentences.zh: 我也没听说过。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么病？

sentences.en: Yeah, so, you know, it is not well known because it's quite rare.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这种病很罕见，所以不太为人所知。

sentences.en: So the outcomes can be quite variable.
sentences.zh: 预后情况也大不相同。

sentences.en: But we know it's associated with mental illness.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道它与精神疾病有关。

sentences.en: It's associated with significant developmental delays.
sentences.zh: 它与严重的生长发育迟缓有关。

sentences.en: And there really is very little chance of independent living as an adult for people who have this condition.
sentences.zh: 而且患有这种病的人，成年后能够独立生活的几率确实非常小。

sentences.en: and she, you know, went home, her husband rushed home from work and they sit down on the couch and she's, you know, crying as she's saying, we might have to think about
sentences.zh: 她回到家，丈夫也从单位匆匆赶回，他们坐在沙发上，她哭着说，我们可能得考虑

sentences.en: terminating this pregnancy that we really, really wanted.
sentences.zh: 终止这次我们非常、非常期待的妊娠。

sentences.en: And so for Yael, her next steps move actually pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 对于雅艾尔（Yael）来说，接下来的步骤进展得非常快。

sentences.en: She is able to get an appointment for a diagnostic test, something that's going to give her a more definitive result the next day.
sentences.zh: 她第二天就预约到了诊断性检查，这能给她一个更明确的结果。

sentences.en: And it's a test that involves basically sticking a very large needle into her placenta and pulling out a bit of tissue.
sentences.zh: 这项检查基本上就是把一根很粗的针扎进胎盘，取出一点组织。

sentences.en: She found it pretty painful.
sentences.zh: 她觉得非常痛苦。

sentences.en: She had to take a few days to rest in bed.
sentences.zh: 她不得不卧床休息了几天。

sentences.en: Her toddler was asking about the boo-boo on her stomach.
sentences.zh: 她蹒跚学步的孩子问她肚子上的伤口是怎么回事。

sentences.en: And then they wait.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就开始等待。

sentences.en: They wait to get the results and see what's happening.
sentences.zh: 等待结果，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: And it's a pretty agonizing time to not know which way this is going to go.
sentences.zh: 在不知道结果会走向何方的情况下，这段时间非常煎熬。

sentences.en: And then they finally, about two weeks later, get the phone call that it turns out the original result looks to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 大约两周后，他们终于接到电话，说最初的结果似乎是错的。

sentences.en: And that their future child does not have
sentences.zh: 他们未来的孩子并没有

sentences.en: Prader-Willi's syndrome.
sentences.zh: 患有普拉德-威利综合征。

sentences.en: And, you know, they were quite relieved.
sentences.zh: 他们感到非常宽慰。

sentences.en: But, you know, again, describe it as a really, really challenging experience to have gone through.
sentences.zh: 但正如她所说，这确实是一次非常、非常具有挑战性的经历。

sentences.en: And, yeah,
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: Elle's wait was actually pretty short.
sentences.zh: 艾尔（Elle）的等待时间其实很短。

sentences.en: You know, most of the women I talked to had to wait, you know, a month or longer, in some cases, two months to get their follow-up testing done and learn if this original result
sentences.zh: 我采访的大多数女性都不得不等待一个月甚至更久，有些案例甚至要等两个月才能完成后续检查，并得知最初的结果

sentences.en: was right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 是对还是错。

sentences.en: And that's a really long time to kind of sit with this kind of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 在这种不确定性中煎熬，时间真的太漫长了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, they describe some taking time off of school or work because they just couldn't focus, the lost income that came along with that.
sentences.zh: 她们说有些人不得不请假或停工，因为她们根本无法集中精力，随之而来的是收入损失。

sentences.en: Some spent thousands of dollars on their follow-up testing for things that their insurance companies wouldn't cover.
sentences.zh: 有些人花了数千美元进行后续检查，而这些项目保险公司并不承保。

sentences.en: You know, they tried to hide their pregnancies, wearing baggy clothes to, you know, not let people know because in some of these cases that they're testing for,
sentences.zh: 她们试图隐藏怀孕的事实，穿着宽松的衣服，不让别人知道，因为在她们接受筛查的某些疾病中，

sentences.en: the infant mortality rate is incredibly high.
sentences.zh: 婴儿死亡率极高。

sentences.en: So the stakes are really quite high of, you know, the type of things they're testing for.
sentences.zh: 所以她们所筛查的这些疾病，风险确实非常高。

sentences.en: And we do know some portion that's likely quite small but does exist don't get that follow-up testing that they are supposed to.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，有一小部分人——可能比例很小，但确实存在——没有进行她们本该进行的后续检查。

sentences.en: In, you know, doing my reporting for this story, I talked to three geneticists who were involved with cases where someone screened positive on one of the tests I was writing about
sentences.zh: 在为这篇报道做调查时，我采访了三位遗传学家，他们参与的案例中，有人在其中一项我正在撰写的测试中呈阳性，

sentences.en: and terminated a pregnancy before, either before or with never getting a diagnostic test afterwards.
sentences.zh: 并在之后从未进行过诊断性检查的情况下，就终止了妊娠。

sentences.en: Again, we do not think this is the dominant experience but we've seen it documented in some academic literature, in a previous investigation and in my own reporting.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们认为这并非普遍现象，但在一些学术文献、之前的调查以及我自己的报道中，确实有相关记录。

sentences.en: So you're saying that in some rare instances women actually terminated their pregnancy under what is essentially false pretenses given bad information.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，在某些罕见的情况下，女性实际上是在基于错误信息、本质上是虚假前提的情况下终止了妊娠。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's possible some women face a really wrenching choice about whether they can wait as abortion laws get more restrictive.
sentences.zh: 而且，随着堕胎法律变得越来越严格，一些女性可能面临着是否能等待的痛苦抉择。

sentences.en: This type of test is usually done about 10 weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 这类检查通常在怀孕10周左右进行。

sentences.en: An amniocentesis can't be performed.
sentences.zh: 而羊膜穿刺术无法进行。

sentences.en: That's commonly the diagnostic test until 15 or 16 weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 那通常是怀孕15或16周才能做的诊断性检查。

sentences.en: In that time, some women with more restrictive abortion laws, you know, things might change about whether they can obtain an abortion or not.
sentences.zh: 在这段时间里，对于一些处于堕胎法律更严格地区的女性来说，她们能否获得堕胎服务可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: And, you know, I spoke with another woman who lives in Indiana who talked about really struggling to schedule all the diagnostic follow-up testing before her state's
sentences.zh: 我采访了另一位住在印第安纳州的女性，她谈到在州内

sentences.en: abortion ban began.
sentences.zh: 堕胎禁令生效前，她为了预约所有的后续诊断检查而苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And even, you know, gaming out plans if I do have to terminate this pregnancy, what state am I going to drive to in order to be able to do that?
sentences.zh: 甚至还要预想方案：如果我真的必须终止妊娠，我该开车去哪个州才能做到？

sentences.en: And even the people who do get a diagnostic test, they find out it's a false positive, their baby doesn't have the condition it's screened positive for, some of them say
sentences.zh: 即使是那些确实做了诊断检查、发现是假阳性、孩子并没有筛查出的那种疾病的人，有些人也说

sentences.en: the experience really still lingers.
sentences.zh: 那种经历依然挥之不去。

sentences.en: You know, I talked to two new moms who develop postpartum depression and both of them really attributed it to kind of the stress of going through this experience of thinking
sentences.zh: 我采访了两位刚生完孩子的新手妈妈，她们都患上了产后抑郁症，她们都将其归因于经历过那种以为

sentences.en: that their baby had a pretty significant disorder.
sentences.zh: 自己的孩子患有严重疾病的压力。

sentences.en: I talked to a new mom who has a 10-month-old who initially screened positive for a disorder, later learned that it was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位有10个月大宝宝的新手妈妈，她最初筛查呈阳性，后来得知结果是错的。

sentences.en: She said she sometimes finds herself
sentences.zh: 她说她有时会发现自己

sentences.en: Googling the symptoms for whatever month old he is of that disorder.
sentences.zh: 在谷歌上搜索孩子现在这个月龄对应的疾病症状。

sentences.en: She wonders in the back of her head if the initial screening was wrong.
sentences.zh: 她心里总在怀疑，最初的筛查是不是真的错了。

sentences.en: Well, maybe the diagnostic test was wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许是诊断检查错了。

sentences.en: And she says, you know, I know it sounds a little crazy.
sentences.zh: 她说，我知道这听起来有点疯狂。

sentences.en: You know, I hope I stop doing this kind of Googling soon.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能尽快停止这种搜索。

sentences.en: But it just really stays in the back of my mind that it feels like some kind of possibility that was introduced into my child's future.
sentences.zh: 但这真的留在了我的脑海深处，感觉就像是给孩子的未来引入了一种可能性。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: these screenings introduce something that has such a potentially big impact on these women at such a fraught time, but do so with such little accuracy.
sentences.zh: 这些筛查在如此关键的时刻，给这些女性带来了如此巨大的潜在影响，但准确率却如此之低。

sentences.en: Did the company speak to this kind of emotional question?
sentences.zh: 公司方面对这种情感层面的问题有回应吗？

sentences.en: Did they recognize that this isn't just a small thing, that they're introducing a really big variable into these folks' lives without, you know, emotional accuracy?
sentences.zh: 他们是否意识到这不仅仅是一件小事，他们是在没有情感准确性的情况下，给这些人的生活引入了一个非常大的变量？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the thing I heard a lot from the companies is that there should be this whole universe that's around those tests, that there should be genetic counseling
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为我从这些公司听到最多的是，这些测试周围应该有一个完整的体系，应该有遗传咨询

sentences.en: before you get the test, there should be informed consent by the doctor saying,
sentences.zh: 在检查前，医生应该进行知情同意，说明：

sentences.en: I'm testing you for these things, and that afterwards, everyone should have access to some kind of genetic counseling if they do get a positive result that can walk them
sentences.zh: 我正在为你做这些检查，而且事后，如果她们确实得到了阳性结果，每个人都应该能够获得某种遗传咨询，以引导她们

sentences.en: through what this actually means.
sentences.zh: 了解这意味着什么。

sentences.en: In practice, though, that universe just doesn't seem to exist for a lot of women who are getting positive results.
sentences.zh: 然而在实践中，对于许多得到阳性结果的女性来说，这个体系似乎根本不存在。

sentences.en: We're finding that they are, you know, done in quick prenatal appointments.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这些检查是在匆忙的产前预约中完成的。

sentences.en: You know, some doctors decide not to run these tests because they find them quite unreliable.
sentences.zh: 有些医生决定不做这些检查，因为他们觉得这些检查非常不可靠。

sentences.en: I talked to a number who said, I would not use this on my patients, and some of those who do, we, you know, found in our reporting talking to patients just didn't seem
sentences.zh: 我采访了一些医生，他们说，我不会在我的病人身上使用这个，而那些使用它的医生，我们在报道中采访病人时发现，他们似乎

sentences.en: to understand what exactly a positive result on this test meant.
sentences.zh: 并不完全理解这个测试的阳性结果到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: You also see doctors operating in an ecosystem where they are dealing with advertising that former FDA officials tell us is misleading, raises red flags, in one case,
sentences.zh: 你还会看到医生在这样一个生态系统中运作：他们面对的广告，据前FDA官员告诉我们，是具有误导性的，会引发警示；在一个案例中，

sentences.en: an ad for doctors with numbers that were described as meaningless by a former FDA official.
sentences.zh: 一个针对医生的广告中，其数据被一位前FDA官员描述为毫无意义。

sentences.en: So they're in a universe where the advertising isn't regulated.
sentences.zh: 所以他们处于一个广告不受监管的环境中。

sentences.en: They're ordering a lot of tests for their patients and might not fully understand what it means when one of them comes positive for the test that we're writing about.
sentences.zh: 他们为病人开了大量的检查，可能并不完全理解当其中一项检查结果呈阳性时意味着什么。

sentences.en: How is it possible that such an inaccurate test is allowed to be marketed to doctors in the first place or is allowed to be marketed to patients as something that should give
sentences.zh: 这种不准确的检查怎么可能被允许首先向医生推销，或者被允许作为一种能给病人带来

sentences.en: them peace of mind?
sentences.zh: 心理安慰的东西向病人推销？

sentences.en: I feel like we have a highly regulated medical industry.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们有一个监管严格的医疗行业。

sentences.en: How can this happen?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能发生？

sentences.en: Yeah, so these tests exist in a world where they do not get
sentences.zh: 是的，这些测试存在于一个它们无法获得

sentences.en: Food and Drug
sentences.zh: 食品药品

sentences.en: Administration
sentences.zh: 监督管理局（FDA）批准的世界里，

sentences.en: tests and MRIs and all the sorts of other things we get in doctor offices.
sentences.zh: 不像我们在医生办公室做的其他检查和核磁共振那样。

sentences.en: They're what's known as a laboratory developed teSt.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为实验室自研测试（LDT）。

sentences.en: A test that was made in a laboratory is run in that same laboratory and for kind of wonky historical reasons these tests are exempt from
sentences.zh: 一种在实验室里制造、并在同一个实验室运行的测试，由于一些奇怪的历史原因，这些测试免于

sentences.en: FDA oversight which means there's no one really reviewing the claiMs.
sentences.zh: FDA的监管，这意味着没有人真正审查这些声明。

sentences.en: There's no one looking over the data behind these tests to say are the claims about what they're saying accurate?
sentences.zh: 没有人查看这些测试背后的数据，来判断它们所说的声明是否准确。

sentences.en: It's basically test makers designing their studies creating data and deciding how they want to describe that data to patients and doctors.
sentences.zh: 基本上是测试制造商设计研究、创建数据，并决定他们想如何向病人和医生描述这些数据。

sentences.en: You know it's giving
sentences.zh: 这真的很有

sentences.en: Theranos vibes.
sentences.zh: Theranos公司的既视感。

sentences.en: I mean how is this not what you're describing just a big loophole?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你描述的这不就是一个巨大的漏洞吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I want to be clear again this is not
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我想再次澄清，这并不是

sentences.en: Theranos.
sentences.zh: Theranos。

sentences.en: The down screening is a good product that a lot of obstetricians really think is a great development but when you get into these newer tests there are a lot of obstetricians
sentences.zh: 唐氏综合征筛查是一个很好的产品，许多产科医生确实认为这是一个伟大的进步，但当你接触到这些较新的测试时，有很多产科医生

sentences.en: and geneticists that are questioning their value and at the end of the day it leads to some important diagnoses for cases where they find true positives but a lot of anguish
sentences.zh: 和遗传学家都在质疑它们的价值。归根结底，它们确实能为发现真阳性的病例提供重要的诊断，但对于那些比真阳性更常见的假阳性结果的女性来说，却带来了极大的痛苦

sentences.en: and a lot of stress for the women who are getting the false positives that are more common than the true ones.
sentences.zh: 和巨大的压力。

sentences.en: So what should folks take away from that?
sentences.zh: 那么人们应该从中吸取什么教训呢？
